SOP-PROD-01 · Operation-Wise Production

How to Run Operation-Wise Production

End-to-end guide covering three stages: creating a multi-operation Bill of Operations (BOO) in SAP Business ByDesign, linking it to a Production Model, and then creating & confirming the resulting Production Order operation-by-operation in the Materials Hub app.

ⓘ

This flow lets a single finished product go through multiple physical operations (e.g. Blanking, then Bending) as separate, trackable confirmation steps - with the input raw material consumed at the first operation, and the finished output only posted once the final operation is confirmed. Work in between is tracked as WIP.

✓

Live example used throughout this document (real data): Product 100162723-5, Production Model 100162723-5_2 — GSM Bracket OPERATION, Site P2, Quantity 5 EA. Bill of Operations screens below come from SAP directly; the Production Confirmation screens were captured live while creating Production Order / Lot 73309 end-to-end.

PART A

Create the Bill of Operations (BOO) in SAP

Defines the operation sequence (e.g. Blanking → Bending) and the Reporting Points in between where confirmations will happen.

  1. 1

    Open Bills of Operation and click New

    Go to the Production work center → Bills of Operation view, then click New to start a fresh BOO.

  2. 2

    Fill in the General tab

    Enter the BOO ID, Description, Site, Quantity, and the Task-Generation Method (choose the option that generates a task per Operation including Reporting Point, e.g. 'Operation Including Reporting Point').

  3. 3

    Move to the Structure tab and insert each Operation

    Click Insert to add the first Operation (e.g. OP_10 - Blanking + Punching) and enter its parameters (Resource, standard values, etc.) as usual for your process.

    Click Insert again to add the next Operation (e.g. OP_20 - Bending) and enter its parameters the same way. Repeat until every Operation and the Reporting Point Marks between them (START → OP_10 → RP_10 → OP_20 → END) are all in place.

    Tip: each Mark element (START / RP_10 / END) is where a confirmation can happen later in the Materials Hub app - one Mark per stage you want staff to confirm separately.
  4. 4

    Save and Check Consistency

    Click Save, then run Check Consistency to confirm SAP accepts the structure with no errors before moving on.

PART B

Create the Production Model

Links a Product ID to the BOO above and to the raw material Bill of Material, at a specific Site.

  1. 5

    Open Production Model and click New

    Go to Production Model → click New. Enter the Product ID, fill in the Planning Area, and set Valid From to a date always in the past relative to today (e.g. if today is 15-09, set Valid From to 01-09). Set both the Minimum and Maximum Lot Size.

  2. 6

    Link the Bill of Operations and Finish

    Move to the Bill of Operations tab, select the BOO ID you created in Part A, then click Finish.

  3. 7

    Edit the Production Model to assign the input material to the first Operation

    Open the saved Production Model in Edit mode, go to Bill of Operations → Product Assignment, and assign your BOM line item (the raw material input) under the first Operation's Produce Activity - so it is consumed as soon as that operation is complete, not at the end.

    If you don't explicitly assign a line item group to an Activity, SAP automatically assigns all input products to the first Produce Activity in the Bill of Operations - so this is usually already correct, just verify it here.
  4. 8

    Release and Save

    Click Release Production Model, then Save. The model is now ready to be used for a Production Order.

PART C

Create & Confirm the Production Order (Materials Hub app)

This is where staff actually run the job day to day - creating the order, then confirming each operation as it's physically completed.

  1. 9

    Create Production Order → enter the Product ID

    Open Production Confirmation (Test) in the app, stay on the Create Production Order tab, and type the Product ID.

  2. 10

    Pick the Production Model, confirm Site, set Quantity

    Choose the matching Production Model from the Source of Supply dropdown (Site auto-fills from it), then set the Quantity to produce.

  3. 11

    Click Create Production Order

    Click Create Production Order. This runs fully automated in the background (checking stock, creating the SAP proposal, then releasing it) and is tracked in the Active Orders table so the form is free to submit another right away.

  4. 12

    Look up the Production Order in Production Confirmation

    Switch to the Production Confirmation tab and look up the new Production Order / Lot ID (use Manual Lot ID lookup if it hasn't appeared in the list yet). You'll see one row per Operation-wise Reporting Point for this lot.

    Real example: Lot 73309 shows two rows - OP_10 - BLANK+PUNCHING (first operation) and OP_20 - BENDING (final operation).
  5. 13

    Confirm the first operation - scrap posts and input material is consumed

    Click Confirm on the first row. Enter the Confirmed Output Quantity; record any Scrap if applicable. Leave Mark as Finished unchecked - the job isn't done yet, it just moves to the next operation. Posting here is what triggers SAP to backflush-consume the raw material input.

  6. 14

    Result: quantity moves forward to the next operation

    After posting, the first row's Open quantity drops to 0, and the second row's Awaiting Prev Step column now shows the quantity that has cleared and is ready to confirm next.

  7. 15

    Confirm the final operation - output is received and WIP clears

    Click Confirm on the second/final row. Enter the Confirmed Output Quantity, and this time check Mark as Finished since this is the last operation. Posting this receives the finished output into stock and clears the Work-in-Process (WIP) that was sitting between the two confirmations.

  8. 16

    Done - the lot is fully finished

    The lot now shows both operations Confirmed, the final row marked Finished = Yes, and the Last Confirmation column showing Posted / Full / WIP Pending → Cleared.
